entries.text: Netflix would have given this project one more season before canceling it, but you have better judgment.
The print was pulled from production before the trailer could generate any interest.
The stop button just delivered the shortest performance review in industrial history.
The project reached the rare milestone of becoming a discontinued product before becoming a product.
The cancellation has been received by the filament with the same enthusiasm as a canceled Monday meeting.
The printer has been granted a recess while the business case is reexamined.
The production crew has been sent home and the unfinished prop is not eligible for a sequel.
The stop button has finally justified its existence more convincingly than the start button did.
A venture capitalist would call this a pivot and immediately try to raise more money.
The printer has discovered a new production method called cutting your losses before they multiply.
The project has been taken off the schedule before anyone could sell tickets.
The build plate has been relieved of a contractual obligation to manufacture this particular decision.
The manufacturing equivalent of deleting an online shopping cart after seeing the shipping charge.
The only thing discontinued faster was the optimism present at the start of the print.
The cancellation notice arrived before the project could become a regular item on the household expense report.
The printer was preparing a full length feature and you wisely released it as a short.
The project got the same treatment as a restaurant reservation made during an argument.

The stop button is the only part of this project that can claim a decisive victory.

The project is now a limited edition of zero completed units.

The printer was about to make history and instead received a sensible administrative decision.
A canceled print is a financial intervention performed by the same person who caused the financial problem.
The model has been granted the rare privilege of remaining significantly cheaper as a computer file.
The production team has been told to return its equipment and stop pitching sequels.
The printer has received a cease and desist from the last surviving sensible impulse in the room.
The cancellation department has finally demonstrated a higher rate of productivity than the manufacturing department.
The project was withdrawn before it could qualify for an extended warranty nobody would buy.
The print has been replaced on the schedule by the revolutionary invention of leaving the machine alone.
The stop command has achieved what several centuries of philosophy could not: a convincing argument for restraint.
The original business plan has been revised from producing an object to preserving what's left of the spool.
The printer has been dismissed early without having to pretend it needs the rest of the afternoon.
The project has joined the distinguished ranks of ideas that improved considerably when nobody finished them.
